title: One Edit Distance
statement: Return true if strings s and t differ by exactly one insertion, deletion, or replacement. Examples: s="ab", t="acb" -> true; s="", t="" -> false. Constraints: lengths up to 10^4.
approach_name: Single mismatch with length-aware suffix check

title: Find Peak Element
statement: Return an index of a peak element, where the element is strictly greater than its existing neighbors. Assume nums[-1] and nums[n] are negative infinity. Example: [1,2,3,1] -> 2. Constraints: nums is non-empty and adjacent values differ.

title: Missing Ranges
statement: Given sorted unique values and inclusive lower/upper bounds, return the missing inclusive ranges as strings. Example: nums=[0,1,3,50,75], lower=0, upper=99 -> ["2","4->49","51->74","76->99"].

title: Maximum Gap
statement: Return the maximum difference between adjacent values after sorting the array; return 0 for fewer than two values. Target linear time and space. Example: [3,6,9,1] -> 3.

title: Compare Version Numbers
statement: Compare dotted version strings, treating each component as a non-negative integer and ignoring leading zeroes. Return -1, 0, or 1. Examples: "1.01" vs "1.001" -> 0; "1.0" vs "1.0.0" -> 0.

title: Fraction to Recurring Decimal
statement: Convert numerator/denominator to a decimal string, enclosing a repeating fractional cycle in parentheses. Examples: 1/2 -> "0.5"; 2/3 -> "0.(6)"; 4/333 -> "0.(012)".
approach_name: Track remainders to locate repeating cycle

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
statement: Given a nondecreasing 1-indexed array, return the two 1-based indices whose values sum to target. Exactly one solution exists and an element cannot be reused. Example: [2,7,11,15], target=9 -> [1,2].

title: Two Sum III - Data Structure Design
statement: Design a data structure with add(number) and find(value), where find returns whether any two stored numbers sum to value. Duplicate values may be added and can form a pair. Example: add(1), add(3), add(5); find(4) -> true; find(7) -> false.
